group-cost: Each group counts everything in the groups beneath it. Costs, deaths and harvests belong to the unit they were recorded for.
Open batches and Alive now are as of now, whatever the dates. Feed conversion (FCR) belongs to the unit the batch is in now.
batch-performance: Lists the batches that ran at any time in the dates. Cost, deaths, feed and feed conversion are lifetime-to-date figures, from the batch's start to the To date, not only the dates chosen.
Cost is the feed, medicine and other costs charged to the batch. Average weight is the last weight sample, or the opening weight when none was taken. The total FCR counts only batches with weights.
mortality: Deaths recorded in the dates, highest first (by month in date order). A death belongs to the unit it was recorded for. How much of a loss was beyond the stage allowance is on each batch's Stages tab.
feed: Quantity is in the feed product's own unit. Feed (kg) counts feed whose unit has a mass equivalence on Measurement Units; other feed shows quantity and cost but no kilograms.
Feeding days counts each batch and day once. Feed belongs to the unit it was recorded for. Cost is the stock cost of what was issued.
harvest-output: What left the batches into stock in the dates, by product, with the cost it carried. Cost per unit is the cost of one unit of the product, such as one kg or one egg.
There is no total row because products are in different units. A harvest or collection belongs to the unit it was recorded for.

help.products: The products this species puts into stock, such as eggs for layers or live birds for broilers. Harvest and Collect produce offer only these. Leave empty to allow any product.
help.stages: List the stages in the order a batch passes through them. Normal mortality is the share of a stage's opening count that is expected to be lost; losses beyond it are written off as abnormal. Leave it empty until the rates are confirmed.
help.countLabel: What the animals are called on screens, e.g. fish or birds.
help.depreciation: Depreciation is a straight line over the useful life, down to the value per head at the end. It is added to the cost of the produce collected, so the animals are carried at roughly that value when they are sold or slaughtered.
help.weightUnit: The unit weights are entered and shown in for this species, such as grams for fingerlings and kilograms for cattle. They are stored in grams, so changing it later does not alter any weight already recorded.

feedTrend.title: Feed over the batch
feedTrend.help: Feed given each day from the start of the batch (kilograms, bars) and what it cost (line). Group by week or month to see the trend more clearly. Only feed whose unit has a weight equivalence in Measurement Units is counted in kilograms.
feedTrend.none: No feed has been given to this batch yet.
feedTrend.otherUnits: Not counted in kilograms (no weight equivalence): {units}

fcr.title: Feed conversion (FCR)
fcr.help: Kilograms of feed given for each kilogram of weight gained. Lower is better. Gain is the weight of the animals now, less what they weighed at the start, plus the weight of those harvested or lost along the way. It depends on weighings being kept up to date, and only feed whose unit has a weight equivalence in Measurement Units is counted.
fcr.otherUnits: Feed given in {units} was left out because its unit has no weight equivalence set in Measurement Units.

mortality.title: Record Mortality
mortality.help: Mortality up to the stage's allowance is absorbed into the survivors' cost. Beyond it, you will be asked to write it off.

transfer.title: Move to Another Unit
transfer.help: Only units on the same farm can be used. Moving a batch between farms is not supported yet.

advance.mustMove: {unit} is not set up for the {stage} stage, so the batch must move to a unit that is.
advance.title: Move to the Next Stage
advance.help: The current stage closes at the live count. Optionally move the batch to another unit in the same step.

input.title: Feed / Medication
input.help: Stock is issued at its average cost and charged to the batch. It must be held under the farm's cost center.

expense.title: Add Cost to Batch
expense.help: Moves a cost already booked in another ledger (labour, power, purchase of fry, ...) into the batch.

writeOff.title: Write Off Abnormal Mortality
writeOff.nothing: There is no abnormal mortality to write off.
writeOff.summary: {quantity} {animals} beyond the allowed mortality, at {rate} each
writeOff.help: Normal losses stay in the survivors' cost. This takes only the excess out, as a loss.

produce.title: Collect produce
produce.help: The produce goes into stock at the cost of running the flock since the last collection plus its depreciation. The {animals} stay in the batch.
produce.carried: Value of the animals before this collection
produce.fullyDepreciated: The useful life is used up: nothing more is depreciated.
produce.recalculated: The cost is worked out again when you save, from the batch as it stands without this record.

harvest.title: Harvest
harvest.help: The batch's cost of these {animals} moves into stock. Harvesting every one that remains closes the batch.
harvest.blocked: Write off the abnormal mortality first.

close.title: Close Batch
close.help: Closes a batch with no {animals} left. Any cost still in WIP is written off as a loss.
close.fishLeft: {count} {animals} are still alive. Harvest them before closing the batch.

edit.title: Edit Batch
edit.help: Correct when this batch started, or its remarks. The start can move earlier, but not past the first record on the batch or the start of its second stage.

stageDate.title: Change when {stage} started
stageDate.help: Correct the date this stage began; the stage before it ends on the same date. It must be after the previous stage began and before the next one begins, and no record already made may be left outside its stage. Closed batches cannot be changed.
stageDate.label: Stage start

spread.title: Spread an amount over the batches
spread.help: Fills the lines below from one amount, such as boat fuel, shared over the open batches that have animals on the date of this record: all farm, or only a group and the groups inside it. Equally per cage: every unit takes the same, and a unit with several batches divides its part. By animals alive: more animals, more cost. By biomass: animals alive times their last sampled weight. By feed given: by the cost of feed given in the last days. Nothing is saved until you save the record, and you can change any line first.
